sections.title: local remediation , projections, softmax stability, rotation

keyTerms.definition: A learned linear map. It rotates, scales, and mixes axes.
It subtracts the max before exp. The shift prevents overflow and changes nothing.
Rotary position embedding. It applies 2D rotation per position.

recall.answer: Rotations compose by adding angles, and RoPE applies this fact per position.
recall.question: Why does R(a)R(b) = R(a+b) matter for RoPE?

recall.answer: softmax([0, 1]). The max-shift changes nothing mathematically.
recall.question: What does softmax([1000, 1001]) equal?

keyTerms.definition: phi: R^d -> R^m. It approximates the softmax kernel as an inner product.
The approximation matches exp(q.k) in expectation. Variance is the price.
D. It keeps approximated rows summing to 1.
It uses random features with E[phi(q).phi(k)] = exp(q.k).

recall.answer: It computes S = phi(K)^T V once, then multiplies per query. The product associates right to left.
recall.question: How does linear attention avoid the T x T matrix?

recall.answer: At small m the variance swamps the signal and training diverges. Unbiasedness says nothing about a single run.
recall.question: Why can an unbiased approximation still fail?

keyTerms.definition: Multi-head attention. h parallel heads with private projections, concatenated.
Per-head dimension. d divided by h.
1/sqrt(d_k). It keeps dot products O(1) at init so the softmax starts diffuse.

recall.answer: q.k in 16 dims has variance 16. Dividing by 4 restores unit scale so the softmax starts diffuse.
recall.question: Why divide by sqrt(d_k)?

recall.answer: Heads starve. More heads means thinner heads with less capacity each.
recall.question: What happens past d_k = 32 at fixed d?

keyTerms.definition: Multi-query attention. Many query heads share 1 KV head.
Stored keys and values. MQA shrinks it 32x in the toy.
The number of key/value heads. MQA sets it to 1.

recall.answer: The K and V heads. Queries keep private projections.
recall.question: What is shared in MQA?

recall.answer: Small models trained with MQA underperform MHA. The capacity cut bites when the model is already small.
recall.question: When does MQA sharing hurt?

keyTerms.definition: Grouped-query attention. G groups of query heads share one KV head each.
Group count. G = h is MHA, G = 1 is MQA.
Converting MHA to GQA by mean-pooling KV heads within groups, then continued training.

recall.answer: The number of KV groups. G = h gives MHA, G = 1 gives MQA.
recall.question: What does G control?

recall.answer: Mean-pooling KV heads without it drops quality. The recovery run restores it.
recall.question: Why does free conversion need continued training?

keyTerms.definition: Fixed position codes from sines and cosines. They extend to any length.
The period of a sinusoid pair. Short waves track exact offsets.
Max trained length for learned positions. Past it, rows are garbage.

recall.question: Write the sinusoid formula.

recall.answer: Position T_max + 5 has no trained row. The model sees garbage and generation degrades.
recall.question: Why cannot learned positions extrapolate?

keyTerms.definition: Rotary position embedding. It spins Q/K pairs by angles proportional to position.
Per-pair rotation frequency. Position m rotates pair i by m * theta_i.
The dot product of rotated pairs depends only on the offset n - m.

recall.answer: Only the offset (n - m). No absolute m or n remains.
recall.question: What does the RoPE dot product depend on?

recall.answer: Unseen angle combinations. Perplexity explodes; fixes are larger base or position interpolation.
recall.question: What breaks RoPE past trained length?

keyTerms.definition: It subtracts a per-head slope times distance. No position vector exists.
A learned bucketed bias per offset, added to scores.
Per-head ALiBi slope. Far pairs pay m_h times distance.

recall.answer: B[h,i,j] = -m_h * |i - j|, added to scores before softmax.
recall.question: Write the ALiBi bias.

recall.answer: The rule uses only i - j. It applies at any length, so extrapolation is structural.
recall.question: Why do relative schemes extrapolate?

keyTerms.definition: It reads the whole input bidirectionally. Its mask is all zeros.
It writes left to right with a causal mask.
Decoder queries attend to encoder keys and values.

recall.answer: Encoder: unmasked. Decoder self: causal. Cross: all source positions allowed.
recall.question: Draw the three masks.

recall.answer: Its bidirectional targets would leak the future. Generation needs causal masks.
recall.question: Why cannot BERT generate left to right?

keyTerms.definition: Masked language modeling. Hide 15% of tokens, predict them from context.
Next-sentence prediction. RoBERTa dropped it with no loss.
A small student matches the teacher soft targets plus true labels.
The teacher uncertainty in soft targets. The student learns from it.

recall.answer: MLM predicts masked tokens from both sides. NSP predicts whether sentence B follows A.
recall.question: What do MLM and NSP predict?

recall.answer: No loss. The signal was mostly topic, not order.
recall.question: Why did RoBERTa drop NSP?

keyTerms.definition: It processes the prompt in parallel and writes all K/V.
It appends one token K/V per step and attends over the cache.
Stored keys per layer with shape (B, kv_heads, T_cached, d_k).

recall.answer: K_cache and V_cache: (B, kv_heads, T_cached, d_k).
recall.question: What is stored per layer?

recall.answer: A stale entry serves another user context. Cache keys must include the full prefix identity.
recall.question: What breaks prefix caching?

keyTerms.definition: The attention cost. QK^T and AV each cost T^2 d multiply-adds.
Scores dominate iff T > d. The regime flips at T = d.
It prints QK^T, AV, projections, FFN, and totals. The design tool.

recall.answer: O(T^2 d + T d^2). Scores and AV cost T^2 d, projections cost T d^2.
recall.question: Write the per-layer big-O.

recall.answer: Poor memory locality can beat FLOP savings. Flash Attention keeps FLOPs and cuts IO.
recall.question: Why does fewer FLOPs not mean faster?

keyTerms.definition: Position 0 absorbs mass when nothing matches. Softmax needs a dump.
Token vectors converge toward rank-1. The residual and FFN fight it.
A sharp perplexity rise past trained length. It points at positions.

recall.answer: Extrapolation: perplexity cliff past trained length. Sink: position 0 absorbs mass. Rank collapse: token vectors converge.
